title: Worktree dispatch: harness file tools silently resolve relative paths against the launch cwd
wanted_capability: A first-class working-directory override for dispatched sessions (dispatch-time cwd param, or an in-session chdir/workdir tool affecting file_read/file_edit/content_search and shell default cwd), so a bro instructed to work in a self-created git worktree actually operates there. Today file tools resolve relative paths against the LAUNCH cwd: in a 4-bro worktree fan-out, one bro silently edited five files in the primary checkout mid-flight (caught by orchestrator IDE diagnostics + steer), a second applied edits to primary AND made an accidental commit there before self-correcting, and a third only avoided it because the shell layer rejected a ../ escape loudly, forcing absolute paths. Silent-wrong-tree is a data-hazard class: it defeats worktree isolation and risks clobbering peer/orchestrator state in the primary tree.
missing_primitive: dispatch-time cwd override / session workdir tool
fallback_used: Brief-level instruction to use absolute paths + --manifest-path/--target-dir pinning on every cargo command; orchestrator mid-run bro_steer recovery (copy-to-worktree + git checkout -- restore of primary) when a bro falls into the trap.
evidence: wave-7 fan-out thread-9dfe1da5: W7b narration 'changes were applied to the primary checkout... commit went to the primary checkout... undo the accidental commit'
W7c live-caught editing 5 primary files (bro-protocol/fleet-client/orchestration/roster) while briefed into ../ts-w7c
W7a narration: shell helper refused relative ../ts-w7a wd escape; succeeded only via absolute paths + manifest-path pinning
